scope: Independent reading of six actual answers and recognized prompts, checked against primary memory-model sources. No CUDA compilation/execution or human interview certification.

findings.finding: The answer clarifies stale results versus a hang and asks for a minimal reproducer. The examiner demands a broader validation/tracing checklist than the public request for what to clarify first; its incomplete grade is not a decisive failure of the opening.
A visible active kernel is not proof of useful forward progress. The next adaptive question drills into that distinction; the broad timeline outline does not establish a validated liveness diagnosis.
Repeated advancing milestones support progress, while unchanged observations alone do not prove deadlock. Safe concurrent observation was not specified here and is addressed by later questions.

The answer names system scope and release/acquire but does not supply the requested concrete host-load mechanism or exact concurrent-access capability conditions. Incomplete; neither mapped nor managed memory implies arbitrary host/GPU atomic interoperability.

The described mapped-memory RMW path requires appropriate native atomic support, alignment, lifetime and compatible host atomic operations. The answer leaves capability queries abstract and uses GCC-style host builtins that are not portable to MSVC. It does not establish a complete portable CUDA implementation. Flat samples alone do not falsify visibility unless independent evidence establishes the updates occurred and the observation assumptions hold.

Incorrect synchronization trace: assuming valid system-scope operations, the two adjacent release RMWs form a release sequence. An acquire reading the second RMW can synchronize with the first release as well as the second, so both publishing threads� prior payload writes happen before the host reads. This requires initialization to zero, the stipulated two increments/no resets or intervening sequence-breaking stores, accessible payload memory and no later conflicting writes. Cross-CTA payload writers must themselves be ordered before their publishing thread. Separate per-CTA flags are an explicit alternative, not a fix required by the stated two-RMW protocol.
